title: Preflight risk scrub and hotfix sprint notes
content:
Meeting: Preflight risk scrub + hotfix sprint planning
Date: 2026-03-10
Facilitator: Avery Chen
Attendees: Marco R., Priya P., Janelle K., Ravi S., SRE on-call (Ben), QA lead (Maya)

Purpose:
- Quick risk triage for the upcoming release train (week 11) and identify any hotfix candidates to triage into next sprint.
- Confirm canary plan, rollback criteria, and communication cadence.
- Reconcile capacity (Dedicated pools) against expected surge for big model rollout.

Agenda:
1) High-level pass on release contents and risk areas (5–10 min)
2) Hotfix candidate review and prioritization (15 min)
3) Canary metric thresholds + alerting + rollback plan (15 min)
4) Capacity & GPU pool dry-run checks (10 min)
5) Ops comms and owner assignments (5–10 min)

Notes / Decisions:
- Release contents: model-variant v2.3.1, runtime kernel bump (cuda-14 opt), routing policy change to favor cheaper regions for non-SLA customers.
- Primary risk vectors: quantization regression for long-context prompts, cache invalidation producing higher latencies in dedicated pools, and a non-deterministic failure mode seen in kcache eviction on a subset of instances.
- Decision: proceed with release train but gate by canary success criteria (see below). If any canary metric breaches twice in a row within 30m window, pause rollout and trigger rollback.

Hotfix candidates (triage ranking):
- HF-1 (P0): kcache eviction leading to 50–100ms latency spikes for cached requests on dedicated-gpu-pool-3. Repro on staging with heavy KV cache churn. Owner: Marco R. ETA: 48h for mitigation patch and canary.
- HF-2 (P1): occasional tokenization mismatch for certain emoji sequences after tokenizer upgrade. Owner: Priya P. ETA: 72h for patch + tests.
- HF-3 (P2): console dashboard misreporting per-route cost in certain timezones (US/CET overlap). Low customer impact; schedule for next sprint. Owner: Janelle K.

Canary plan and metrics (hard gates):
- Canary cohort: 1% of traffic routed to v2.3.1 (hosted) + 2 small Dedicated instances (dedicated-gpu-pool-canary-a/b). Duration: initial 60m, then 4h progressive increase if stable.
- Success thresholds:
  - p95 latency increase <= 10% vs baseline
  - error rate (5xx) <= baseline + 0.1% absolute
  - average tokens/sec throughput within -15% of baseline for dedicated pools
  - model correctness quick-check: 30 synthetic prompt evals with 0 regressions allowed (run by QA)
- Canary alerting: PagerDuty on-call (SRE) if any threshold breached; Slack #release-ops alert with summary.
- Rollback criteria: any two threshold breaches within 30m OR a single P0 bug in canary. Rollback procedure documented in linked Confluence page.

Capacity & pool notes:
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated-gpu-pool-2 at 85% baseline during batch jobs; planned to shift 2 reserved slots from non-prod to prod for rollout window. Ops to do slot rebind at +2h before rollout. Owner: Ravi S.
- Burst capacity policy: enable burst on dedicated-gpu-pool-1 only if canary passes 4h mark. Confirm billing impact with finance before enabling. Action: Ravi to confirm by EOD 2026-03-11.

Test artifacts & quick checks:
- QA to run the stability harness against long-context workloads (seq_len 16k) — Maya to post results in Slack.
- Perf script: github.com/redwood-inference/release-scripts#canary-perf-run — run w/ seed=20260310 and attach logs.

Communication plan:
- Pre-rollout (T-2h): Slack #release-ops post with expected changes, owners, and rollback plan. PagerDuty: passive watch.
- Rollout start: send to #all-eng and #gpm a short note with canary cohort size and expected window.
- If canary passes 4h: send green update and schedule progressive rollout.
- If rollback: immediate incident channel (#prod-incident) and set 1h postmortem runbook.

Action items (owner / due):
- Marco R.: create kcache mitigation PR & test matrix (due 2026-03-12)
- Priya P.: full tokenizer regression test + hotfix branch (due 2026-03-13)
- Ravi S.: adjust dedicated pool slot binding + confirm burst billing (due 2026-03-11)
- Maya (QA): run long-context harness and post failures + golden set comparisons (due 2026-03-11)
- Avery: draft canary announcement and Slack template + update Confluence preflight doc (due 2026-03-11)

Open questions / risks to watch:
- Is the synthetic eval suite covering the new quantization edge cases? If not, which prompts are missing? (Action: Priya to update prompt set)
- Does our tracing provide enough sample-level context to debug kcache evictions across nodes? If not, add span tags. (Action: Marco + SRE)
- Backup plan if Dedicated pool capacity is insufficient during peak: fallback to hosted lightweight variant (v2.3.1-small) with degraded throughput and documented SLO hit. Need product sign-off.

Retro / notes for next preflight:
- Start a mini dry-run 48h earlier for any runtime/kernel changes to give time for hotfixes.
- Improve ownership clarity on capacity ops (single comms owner for the window).
- Add automated canary-verdict runner that posts to Slack and opens a rollback PR automatically if thresholds breach.

Next meeting: quick sync T-1 (30m) on 2026-03-12 morning to confirm all action items closed and canary artifacts uploaded.

End of notes.
